title: docs(tests): make the network-escape guard's Fix: text say where the teardown goes
body:
Fixes #7765

The network-escape guard's failure message is this repo's canonical instruction
for the class, and objectui#7307 is a 21-file burn-down following it. It
prescribed `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', router) + vi.unstubAllGlobals()` and said
nothing about **where** the unstub goes — and that omission is what made
objectui#7439 flake. This changes what the guard **says**, not what it catches.

## The new wording, and the passage it follows

Card objectui#7765 required the new clause to follow the worked example landed in
PR objectui#7764 rather than invent a second explanation, "because the defect
class this card belongs to is one ruling written twice, and one copy rotting."
The passage followed is the module-scope comment in
`packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.approvalDeclaredActions.test.tsx`
(lines 286-312). Its load-bearing sentences, and where each landed:

| objectui#7764 comment | guard message now says |
|---|---|
| "Vitest runs `afterEach` hooks in reverse registration order, so a teardown in THIS file runs FIRST — before the root setup's RTL `cleanup()` and before the network-escape guard's assertion" | same sentence, trimmed to "before this assertion" |
| "installed ONCE, here at module scope, and is deliberately NEVER torn down" | "Install ONE at module scope and leave it up for the whole file" |
| "no test can ever end with the real `fetch` back in place" | verbatim |
| "any `refreshAfter`... `notifyDataChanged`... Both are fire-and-forget by design: nothing in the console awaits them, and no test barrier here waits for them either" | "any refreshAfter, any notifyDataChanged consumer, any fire-and-forget refresh no barrier awaits" |

One clause is **not** from objectui#7764. The referenced example the message has
always pointed at,
`packages/plugin-report/src/__tests__/DatasetReportRenderer.test.tsx`, already
hardened its own teardown: its `afterEach` (lines 137-148) calls `cleanup()`
**before** `vi.unstubAllGlobals()`, with a comment stating the same reverse-order
fact and its own measurement — "Measured — one run in six leaked a single
attempt that way." That ordering is the cheaper of the two remedies and was
being dropped on the floor by the message's one-line summary of that file, so it
is now the first bullet. It is quoted from the file the message already cites,
not invented here.

## The second copy — named individually

The claim's file surface admitted sibling guards printing the same prescription,
"but name each one." There is exactly one:
`scripts/__tests__/network-escape-ledger.test.ts` (lines 76-78) restated the
shape in its own ledger-GREW assertion message. Restating the new clause there
would have recreated the very defect this card is about, so that message now
**points at** the guard's text instead of carrying a second copy of it.

Nothing asserts on the guard's message text: the only importer of the guard is
that pin, and it imports `KNOWN_ESCAPES` (the set), not the string.

## Void condition — not tripped

Clause-② is `no`, so any change to the guard's **verdict** voids the card.

- `KNOWN_ESCAPES` untouched, and the four prohibitions all held.
- Mechanically checked, not asserted: lines 110-235 of the guard — the whole
  `KNOWN_ESCAPES` set, `guardedFetch`, and the `afterEach` filter and verdict —
  `diff` byte-identical against `origin/main`. The single changed hunk is
  `@@ -239,2 +239,18 @@`, inside the `throw new Error(...)` template literal.
- No file under `packages/*/src` changed. Diff is 2 files, anchored on the
  recorded base `dfcbedee5` (`origin/main` advanced to `7c67a773` mid-run, so a
  two-dot diff would have credited this branch with a sibling's merge).
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test`: `NOT GOVERNED — 2 path(s) checked
  against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` Kept as draft regardless.

## Lit control — the new text really is on the failure path

Not a static argument: a real escape was provoked and the printed message read
back. A temporary case was appended to
`scripts/__tests__/report-namespace-agreement-6416.test.ts` calling
`fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/lit-control-7765')`, run with a name filter.

Mutation confirmed **on disk before** the run, by hash:

```
HEAD blob:      a60eff61085e7e53a9b241ead7200c87c0c04885
mutated blob:   c82fac446f75e221820de5998a4d930e820bfe35   (non-empty, differs)
```

The guard went red and printed the whole new clause, thrown from
`vitest.setup.network-escape-guard.ts:227`:

```
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 12 skipped (13)

Error: Network escape: this test reached a REAL socket at http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/lit-control-7765.
...
WHERE that pair is torn down is part of the shape, not a detail
(objectui#7439). Vitest runs afterEach hooks in REVERSE registration order,
so a teardown written in THIS file runs FIRST — before the root setup's
RTL cleanup() and before this assertion. ...
  - call cleanup() BEFORE vi.unstubAllGlobals(), as that
    DatasetReportRenderer afterEach already does; and
  - if the component can issue a read AFTER the test body returns — any
    refreshAfter, any notifyDataChanged consumer, any fire-and-forget
    refresh no barrier awaits — do not tear the double down at all.
```

Restoration was under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with an absolute path, but the
proof is **state**, not that the trap fired:

```
HEAD blob:      a60eff61085e7e53a9b241ead7200c87c0c04885
worktree blob:  a60eff61085e7e53a9b241ead7200c87c0c04885   HASH EQUALITY: PASS
marker residue: 0
git diff HEAD:  (empty)          git status: clean
```

## Green readings — the guard is a ROOT setup, so scale matters

It loads through `vitest.setup.base.ts` for every project, so a single file
would not show it undamaged.

| reading | files | tests | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vitest run --project unit` | **905 passed (905)** | **14927 passed, 9 skipped (14936)** | 0 |
| `vitest run --project dom --shard=1/8` | **191 passed (191)** | **1898 passed (1898)** | 0 |
| `vitest run scripts/__tests__/network-escape-ledger.test.ts` (the pin for a file changed here, named) | 1 passed (1) | 3 passed (3) | 0 |

Gates, each read from its own printed verdict rather than a bare `$?`:

- `pnpm type-check:vitest-setup` — **exit 0, no diagnostics.** This is the gate
  for a repo-root setup file; turbo's `type-check` structurally cannot reach one.
  It resolves `@object-ui/components`, `/fields`, `/plugin-dashboard`,
  `/plugin-grid` through their built declarations, so it was run **after**
  building those four closures. Run before that build it emits four `TS2882` —
  an unmet prerequisite, not a result, and not reported as one.
- `pnpm type-check:scripts` — exit 0 (covers the ledger pin file).
- `pnpm lint:root` — exit 0; 33 warnings, 0 errors, all pre-existing
  `no-explicit-any` at lines 172/181/187, none in the changed hunk.
- `node scripts/check-vi-mock-specifiers.mjs` — `OK (4313 tracked source
  file(s)...)`; `node scripts/check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` — `OK 77
  documented symbol(s)...`. These are the only two gate scripts that read either
  changed path.

All heavy runs went through the shared verify lock; the wall-clock figures it
printed are shared-box seconds, not idle-box ones.

## Changeset

Gate verdict, copied verbatim:

```
Compared the working tree with dfcbedee5 (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 0 changeset(s) added.
✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.
```

Acted on that verdict: no changeset added.

## What was NOT measured — stated plainly

- **Card fact 1 was not independently re-measured here.** No probe was
  registered to re-observe `fetch is still the double? false`. What this PR adds
  is *corroboration from a third, independent site*: the
  `DatasetReportRenderer.test.tsx` `afterEach` comment states the same
  reverse-order fact and reports its own measurement ("one run in six"), written
  by a different author than objectui#7764. Three sites now agree; none of the
  three was re-run as an experiment here.
- **Card fact 2 was not confirmed.** The lit control's `fetch` sits inside the
  test body, so the guard naming that test is the ordinary case, not the
  teardown-window misattribution the card describes. Nothing here says anything
  about fact 2 either way.
